nodes.statement_short: Draw Poisson numbers of 0-to-1 and 1-to-0 flips

nodes.name: Cell weights
nodes.statement: (iii) forming cell weights \(W_j^{+}\propto D_j^{+}\) and \(W_j^{-}\propto D_j^{-}\)
nodes.statement_short: Weights proportional to discrepancies

nodes.name: Allocate flips to cells
nodes.statement: (iv) sampling \((L_1^{+},\dots,L_J^{+})\sim\mathrm{Multinomial}(P^{+};W^{+})\) and \((L_1^{-},\dots,L_J^{-})\sim\mathrm{Multinomial}(P^{-};W^{-})\)
nodes.statement_short: Multinomial allocation of flip budgets across cells

nodes.name: Relabel points
nodes.statement: (v) within each cell \(j\), uniformly relabelling \(L_j^{+}\) currently control-labelled points to treatment and \(L_j^{-}\) currently treatment-labelled points to control.
nodes.statement_short: Uniformly relabel the allocated numbers of points in each cell

nodes.name: Predictability of N(t-) indicators
nodes.statement: Since $N$ is adapted, c\`adl\`ag, and simple, $t\mapsto N(t-)$ is predictable and takes integer values with unit jumps. For each $m\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$, the set $\{(t,\omega):N(t-,\omega)=m\}$ is predictable, hence the indicator $t\mapsto \mathbbm{1}\{N(t-)=m\}$ is predictable.
nodes.statement_short: N(t-) is predictable, so the indicators of {N(t-)=m} are predictable

nodes.name: Indicator expansion of sel_r
nodes.statement: On $[t^\ast,T)$ we have the pointwise identity with pairwise disjoint predictable supports \[ \mathrm{sel}_r(t)=\sum_{m=0}^\infty r_{m+1} \mathbbm{1}\{N(t-)=m\}. \] Because the supports are disjoint and for each $(\omega,t)$ exactly one indicator equals $1$, this is a countable pointwise sum of predictable indicators; hence it is predictable.
nodes.statement_short: Write sel_r as a disjoint sum of predictable indicators

nodes.name: Value at event times
nodes.statement: Simplicity implies $N(t_i-)=i-1$, whence $\mathrm{sel}_r(t_i-)=r_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Simplicity gives N(t_i-)=i-1, hence sel_r(t_i-)=r_i

nodes.name: Continuity of log terms
nodes.statement: Fix $u\in[t^\ast,T]$ and $r\in\mathcal R_{\rm path}$. By Assumption~\ref{ass:G1}, $\widehat\lambda_{r_i}^r(\gamma_i;\theta)\ge \underline\mu_{\min}$ for all $i$ and $\theta$, so $\theta\mapsto \log\widehat\lambda_{r_i}^r(\gamma_i;\theta)$ is continuous.
nodes.statement_short: Margins (Assumption 9) make the event log-terms continuous

nodes.name: Continuity of compensator and maximum on Theta_circ
nodes.statement: On $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$, Assumption~\ref{ass:G2prime} provides a deterministic bound $K_{\rm win}$ such that $\sum_{k=0}^1\widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta)\le K_{\rm win}$ for all $\tau\in D$, all $\theta\in\Theta_\circ$, and all $r\in\mathcal R_{\rm path}$. Since $\theta\mapsto \widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta)$ is continuous for each $\tau$, dominated convergence (dominated by $K_{\rm win}$ on the finite-measure set $D^{[u]}$) implies continuity of \[ \theta\ \longmapsto\ \int_{D^{[u]}} \sum_{k=0}^1 \widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta)\,\mathrm{d}\tau . \] Therefore $\ell_r^{[u]}$ is continuous on $\Theta_\circ$. Since $\Theta_\circ$ is compact, $\ell_r^{[u]}$ attains a maximum on $\Theta_\circ$.
nodes.statement_short: Window envelope plus dominated convergence give continuity; compactness gives a maximiser

nodes.name: Same on Theta_sc and full window
nodes.statement: The same argument applies on the compact set $\Theta_{\rm sc}=\Theta_\circ\cap B(\theta^\star,r_{\rm sc})$. Finally, taking $u=T$ recovers $\ell_r=\ell_r^{[T]}$.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat on Theta_sc and take u=T

nodes.name: Indicator process
nodes.statement: Define $X_t:=\mathbbm{1}\{t>\sigma\}$. Since $\sigma$ is a stopping time, $\{\sigma\le q\}\in\mathcal F_q$ for all $q$.
nodes.statement_short: Define X_t and use the stopping-time property

nodes.name: Adaptedness
nodes.statement: Moreover, for each $t$, \[ \{X_t=1\}=\{\sigma<t\}=\bigcup_{\substack{q\in\mathbb Q\\ q<t}}\{\sigma\le q\}\in\mathcal F_t, \] so $(X_t)$ is adapted.
nodes.statement_short: Write {X_t=1} as a countable union of F_t sets

nodes.name: Left-continuity implies predictability
nodes.statement: Moreover $X$ is left-continuous: $X_\sigma=0$ and for $t\uparrow\sigma$ we have $X_t=0$. Every adapted left-continuous process is predictable, hence $X$ is predictable.
nodes.statement_short: Adapted left-continuous processes are predictable

nodes.name: Complete-data log-likelihood at r*
nodes.statement: Write $\lambda_k^\star(\tau):=\lambda_k(\tau\mid\mathcal G_{t-};\theta^\star)$ and recall that under $r^\star$ (the true labels) the complete-data log-likelihood is \[ \ell_{r^\star}(\theta)=\sum_{k=0}^1\left(\int_D \log\lambda_k(\tau\mid\mathcal G_{t-};\theta)\,dN_k(\tau) -\int_D \lambda_k(\tau\mid\mathcal G_{t-};\theta)\,d\tau\right). \]
nodes.statement_short: Recall the oracle complete-data log-likelihood

nodes.name: Score at the truth
nodes.statement:
Differentiating and evaluating at $	heta^\star$ gives \[ 
abla \ell_{r^\star}(	heta^\star) =\sum_{k=0}^1\left(\int_D 
abla_	heta\log\lambda_k(	au\mid\mathcal G_{t-};	heta^\star)\,dN_k(	au) -\int_D 
abla_	heta\lambda_k(	au\mid\mathcal G_{t-};	heta^\star)\,d	auight). \]
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate at theta*

nodes.name: Martingale representation of the score
nodes.statement:
Using the Doob--Meyer decomposition $dN_k=dM_k^\star+\lambda_k^\star\,d	au$ and the identity $
abla_	heta\log\lambda_k=(
abla_	heta\lambda_k)/\lambda_k$, we obtain the cancellation \[ \int_D 
abla_	heta\log\lambda_k^\star\,\lambda_k^\star\,d	au =\int_D 
abla_	heta\lambda_k^\star\,d	au, \] hence  egin{equation} 
abla \ell_{r^\star}(	heta^\star) =\sum_{k=0}^1\int_D 
abla_	heta\log\lambda_k^\star(	au)\,dM_k^\star(	au). \end{equation} Dividing by $|D|$ yields the same representation for $
abla f_{r^\star}(	heta^\star)$.
nodes.statement_short: Doob-Meyer cancellation yields the martingale representation (eq. 15)

nodes.name: Coordinate integrands
nodes.statement: Fix a coordinate $j\in\{1,\dots,p\}$ and define the predictable integrand \[ h_{k,j}(\tau):=\partial_{\theta_j}\log\lambda_k^\star(\tau) =\frac{\partial_{\theta_j}\lambda_k^\star(\tau)}{\lambda_k^\star(\tau)}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Define the predictable integrands h_{k,j}

nodes.name: Sup bound H
nodes.statement: By oracle positivity, $\lambda_k^\star(\tau)\ge \underline\lambda_k\ge \underline\lambda_{\min}$, and by the oracle gradient bound in Assumption~\ref{ass:G3}, $\|\nabla_\theta\lambda_k^\star(\tau)\|\le S_\infty$ a.e.; therefore \[ |h_{k,j}(\tau)| \le \frac{\|\nabla_\theta\lambda_k^\star(\tau)\|}{\lambda_k^\star(\tau)} \le \frac{S_\infty}{\underline\lambda_{\min}} =:H. \]
nodes.statement_short: Positivity and gradient bound give |h_{k,j}| <= H

nodes.name: Quadratic characteristic bound
nodes.statement: On the window envelope event $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$ we have $\lambda_k^\star(\tau)\le \lambda^\star(\tau)\le K_{\rm win}$, so the predictable quadratic characteristic of $\int_D h_{k,j}\,dM_k^\star$ satisfies \[ V_{k,j} :=\int_D h_{k,j}(\tau)^2\,\lambda_k^\star(\tau)\,d\tau \le \int_D H^2\,\lambda_k^\star(\tau)\,d\tau \le H^2\,K_{\rm win}\,|D|. \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound V_{k,j} by H^2 K_win |D|

nodes.name: Freedman for each coordinate
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:Freedman} (two-sided form) to the scalar martingale integral $X_{k,j}:=\int_D h_{k,j}\,dM_k^\star$. On $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$, with probability at least $1-2e^{-z_{\rm Fr}}$, \[ |X_{k,j}| \le \frac{H}{3}z_{\rm Fr}+\sqrt{2V_{k,j}z_{\rm Fr}+\frac{H^2}{9}z_{\rm Fr}^2} \le \frac{H}{3}z_{\rm Fr}+\sqrt{2H^2K_{\rm win}|D|\,z_{\rm Fr}+\frac{H^2}{9}z_{\rm Fr}^2}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Apply the two-sided Freedman inequality

nodes.name: Simplify the bound
nodes.statement: Using $\sqrt{a+b}\le \sqrt a+\sqrt b$ and $\sqrt{H^2}=H$ gives \[ |X_{k,j}| \le H\sqrt{2K_{\rm win}|D|\,z_{\rm Fr}}+\frac{2H}{3}z_{\rm Fr}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Use sqrt(a+b) <= sqrt a + sqrt b

nodes.name: Union bound over coordinates
nodes.statement: Now union bound over the $2p$ pairs $(k,j)$ yields that, on $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$, with probability at least $1-4p\,e^{-z_{\rm Fr}}$ the above bound holds simultaneously for all $k\in\{0,1\}$ and $j\in\{1,\dots,p\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Union bound over the 2p pairs (k,j)

nodes.name: Coordinatewise score bound
nodes.statement: On this event, for each coordinate $j$ we combine \eqref{eq:score-mtg-rep} with the triangle inequality: \[ \big|\partial_{\theta_j}\ell_{r^\star}(\theta^\star)\big| =\left|\sum_{k=0}^1 X_{k,j}\right| \le \sum_{k=0}^1|X_{k,j}| \le 2H\sqrt{2K_{\rm win}|D|\,z_{\rm Fr}}+\frac{4H}{3}z_{\rm Fr}. \] Dividing by $|D|$ yields \[ \big|\partial_{\theta_j} f_{r^\star}(\theta^\star)\big| \le 2H\sqrt{\frac{2K_{\rm win}z_{\rm Fr}}{|D|}}+\frac{4H}{3}\frac{z_{\rm Fr}}{|D|}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Combine with the martingale representation and normalise

nodes.name: Norm bound
nodes.statement: Finally, $\|\nabla f\|\le \sqrt p\,\max_j|\partial_{\theta_j} f|$, hence \[ \|\nabla f_{r^\star}(\theta^\star)\| \le \sqrt p\left(2H\sqrt{\frac{2K_{\rm win}z_{\rm Fr}}{|D|}}+\frac{4H}{3}\frac{z_{\rm Fr}}{|D|}\right) \le \frac{8\sqrt{2p}\,S_\infty}{\underline\lambda_{\min}} \left(\sqrt{\frac{K_{\rm win}z_{\rm Fr}}{|D|}}+\frac{z_{\rm Fr}}{|D|}\right), \] which is the claimed bound with the stated choice of $C_{\rm sc}$.
nodes.statement_short: Pass from coordinates to the Euclidean norm, giving C_sc

nodes.name: Predictability of {T<t}
nodes.statement: Write $\mathcal P:=\mathcal P(\mathcal G)$ and $\mathcal B:=\mathcal B(\mathbb R^d)$. Since $T$ is a stopping time, $\{(\omega,t):T(\omega)<t\}\in\mathcal P$ (e.g.\ $t\mapsto \mathbf 1\{t>T\}$ is adapted and left-continuous).
nodes.statement_short: Notation and predictability of {T<t}

nodes.name: Predictability of {t<=T+L}
nodes.statement: Likewise, $T+L$ is a stopping time, hence $\{(\omega,t):T(\omega)+L<t\}=\{t>T+L\}\in\mathcal P$, and therefore $\{(\omega,t):t\le T+L\}\in\mathcal P$ by closure under complements.
nodes.statement_short: Same for T+L and complements

nodes.name: Time set A is predictable
nodes.statement: Also $(\Omega\times(0,u])\in\mathcal P$ since $u$ is deterministic. Thus \[ A:=\{(\omega,t): T<t\le u,\ t\le T+L\}\in\mathcal P. \]
nodes.statement_short: Intersect to get A in P

nodes.name: Measurability of the ball indicator
nodes.statement: The map $(\omega,x)\mapsto \mathbf 1\{\|x-X(\omega)\|\le R\}$ is $\sigma(X)\otimes\mathcal B$-measurable.
nodes.statement_short: The ball indicator is sigma(X) x B-measurable

nodes.name: Restriction to {T<=q}
nodes.statement: Since $X$ is $\mathcal G_T$-measurable, for each rational $q\ge 0$ and each Borel $B\in\mathcal B$, \[ \{X\in B\}\cap\{T\le q\}\in\mathcal G_q, \] so by a monotone-class argument the restriction of $(\omega,x)\mapsto \mathbf 1\{\|x-X(\omega)\|\le R\}$ to $\{T\le q\}$ is $\mathcal G_q\otimes\mathcal B$-measurable.
nodes.statement_short: Monotone class: restriction to {T<=q} is G_q x B-measurable

nodes.name: Set E as countable union
nodes.statement: Now consider \[ E:=\{(\omega,t,x): T(\omega)<t,\ \|x-X(\omega)\|\le R\} = \bigcup_{q\in\mathbb Q_+}\Bigl(\{T\le q\}\cap\{\|x-X\|\le R\}\Bigr)\times(q,\infty). \]
nodes.statement_short: Write E as a countable union over rationals

nodes.name: E is P x B measurable
nodes.statement: Each set $\bigl(\{T\le q\}\cap\{\|x-X\|\le R\}\bigr)\times(q,\infty)$ belongs to $\mathcal P\otimes\mathcal B$ because $\{T\le q\}\cap\{\|x-X\|\le R\}\in\mathcal G_q\otimes\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal P$ is generated by rectangles $F\times(s,t]$ with $F\in\mathcal G_s$. Hence $E\in\mathcal P\otimes\mathcal B$.
nodes.statement_short: Each piece is a predictable rectangle times Borel set

nodes.name: Product of indicators
nodes.statement: Finally, \[ \mathbf 1_{C^{[u]}(T,X)}(\omega,t,x)=\mathbf 1_A(\omega,t)\,\mathbf 1_E(\omega,t,x), \] and since $A\in\mathcal P$ and $E\in\mathcal P\otimes\mathcal B$, we obtain $\mathbf 1_{C^{[u]}(T,X)}\in\mathcal P\otimes\mathcal B$.
nodes.statement_short: The cone indicator is 1_A 1_E, hence P x B measurable

nodes.name: Initialize labels
nodes.statement: \textbf{Initialize:} $r^{(0)}$ (arbitrary; no labels are fixed before the first block).
nodes.statement_short: Arbitrary initial labelling
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Loop over blocks
nodes.statement: \textbf{For $m=0,1,\dots,\mathfrak{T}-1$:}\\ \quad\emph{(E-step on the next block $D_{m+1}$)} Assign labels for events with $u_m<t_i\le u_{m+1}$ sequentially by \eqref{eq:greedy-estep}, keeping labels with $t_j\le u_m$ fixed.\\ \quad\emph{(M-step at the block end)} Update the parameter using the cumulative window $D^{(m+1)}=(t^\ast,u_{m+1}]\times\mathcal S$: \[ \theta^{(m+1)} := \hat\theta_{\Theta_{\rm sc}}^{[u_{m+1}]}\!\big(r^{(m+1)}\big) \in \arg\max_{\theta\in\Theta_{\rm sc}}\ell_{r^{(m+1)}}^{[u_{m+1}]}(\theta). \]
nodes.statement_short: Iterate over blocks of the schedule
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Greedy E-step on next block
nodes.statement: \quad\emph{(E-step on the next block $D_{m+1}$)} Assign labels for events with $u_m<t_i\le u_{m+1}$ sequentially by \eqref{eq:greedy-estep}, keeping labels with $t_j\le u_m$ fixed.
nodes.statement_short: Label new-block events sequentially by the penalised greedy rule
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Localised M-step
nodes.statement: \quad\emph{(M-step at the block end)} Update the parameter using the cumulative window $D^{(m+1)}=(t^\ast,u_{m+1}]\times\mathcal S$: \[ \theta^{(m+1)} := \hat\theta_{\Theta_{\rm sc}}^{[u_{m+1}]}\!\big(r^{(m+1)}\big) \in \arg\max_{\theta\in\Theta_{\rm sc}}\ell_{r^{(m+1)}}^{[u_{m+1}]}(\theta). \]
nodes.statement_short: Maximise the prefix complete-data log-likelihood over Theta_sc
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Output
nodes.statement: \textbf{Output:} $\theta^{(\mathfrak{T})}$ and the (progressively assigned) labels $r^{(\mathfrak{T})}$ on $D$.
nodes.statement_short: Return final parameter and labels
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Old labels
nodes.statement: For indices $i$ with $t_i\le u_m$ we have $r_i^{(m+1)}=r_i^{(m)}$, hence $\mathcal G_{t_i}$-measurability holds by the induction (progressive) hypothesis in Assumption~\ref{ass:G0pred}(b).
nodes.statement_short: Labels from previous blocks are unchanged
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Induction set-up
nodes.statement: Now consider the events in the new block $D_{m+1}$ and list them in increasing time order. We argue by induction over this within-block ordering.
nodes.statement_short: Induct over events of the new block in time order
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Base case
nodes.statement: For the first such event $\gamma_i$ (smallest $t_i$ with $u_m<t_i\le u_{m+1}$), the objective in \eqref{eq:greedy-estep} depends only on: (i) the observed history $\mathcal H_{t_i-}\subset \mathcal G_{t_i}$, (ii) already-fixed past labels $r^{(m+1)}_{1:i-1}$ (which are $\mathcal G_{t_i}$-measurable by construction), and (iii) $\theta^{(m)}$, which is $\mathcal G_{u_m}$-measurable and hence $\mathcal G_{t_i}$-measurable because $u_m<t_i$ and $(\mathcal G_t)$ is increasing. With deterministic tie-breaking, $r_i^{(m+1)}$ is therefore $\mathcal G_{t_i}$-measurable.
nodes.statement_short: The first event's greedy objective uses only G_{t_i}-measurable inputs
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Inductive step
nodes.statement: Assume the claim holds for all earlier events in $D_{m+1}$. For the next event $\gamma_{i'}$ in the block, the greedy objective depends on $\mathcal H_{t_{i'}-}$, the already-chosen labels in the block, and $\theta^{(m)}$, all of which are $\mathcal G_{t_{i'}}$-measurable. Deterministic tie-breaking again yields that $r_{i'}^{(m+1)}$ is $\mathcal G_{t_{i'}}$-measurable. This closes the induction.
nodes.statement_short: Later events depend on earlier chosen labels, all G-measurable
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Two-step plan
nodes.statement: We establish the result in two steps: first, a union bound over a finite net to handle the martingale noise; second, a deterministic Lipschitz extension to cover the entire parameter space $\Theta_\circ$.
nodes.statement_short: Net union bound, then Lipschitz extension
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Parameter net
nodes.statement: Recall the fixed, deterministic $\varepsilon_{\rm net}$-net $\mathcal{N}_{\rm net} \subset \Theta_\circ$ from \cref{sec:assumptions}. For concreteness one may take $\varepsilon_{\rm net}:=|D|^{-2}$ (which satisfies $\varepsilon_{\rm net}\le |D|^{-1}$ for $|D|\ge 1$, which is eventually true). Since $p$ is fixed, $|\mathcal{N}_{\rm net}| \le (C \operatorname{diam}(\Theta_\circ)/\varepsilon_{\rm net})^p$, so $\log N_{\rm net} = O(\log |D|)$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the net with log N_net = O(log|D|)
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Item (i) and predictability
nodes.statement: Item (i) is exactly the event $E_{\rm main}$, whose failure probability is controlled by a finite union bound using the tail bounds in \cref{ass:G0,ass:G2prime,ass:G4,ass:G5,ass:G6,ass:G7prime,ass:G8}. For (ii), we consider the collection of all scalar martingales evaluated by the algorithm at update index \(m\), event index $j$, component $k$, and parameter $\theta$. By Assumption~\ref{ass:G0pred}, for any fixed $\theta \in \mathcal{N}_{\rm net}$, the integrand defining these martingales depends only on the history and is $\mathcal{G}$-predictable on the relevant cumulative window.
nodes.statement_short: Item (i) by union bound; integrands at net points are predictable
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Count Freedman events
nodes.statement: Let $N_{\rm total}$ denote the total number of (two-sided) Freedman inequality tail events that we union bound over. On $E_{\rm act}$, the number of prefix event indices we union over is at most $\sum_{m=1}^{\mathfrak{T}}N^{(m)}\le \mathfrak{T}\,N(D)\le (1+\eta_{\rm act})C_{\rm act}|D|\,\mathfrak{T}$. Each candidate contributes at most $(p+2)$ martingales (two scalar terms in Lemma~\ref{lem:perflip} and $p$ gradient coordinates), and we take a two-sided deviation bound. Therefore, for an absolute constant $c_0$ (absorbing these fixed factors, unions over update indices, and any ancillary Freedman inequality calls included in the master union bound), \[ N_{\rm total}\ \le\ c_0\,(p+2)\,N_{\rm net}\,(1+\eta_{\rm act})C_{\rm act}|D|\,\mathfrak{T}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Count the Freedman tail events on E_act
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Union bound via Freedman
nodes.statement: The parameter $z_{\rm Fr}$ in \eqref{eq:z-def} is chosen so that $e^{-z_{\rm Fr}}$ dominates $N_{\rm total}^{-1}$ (up to the extra $|D|^{-\eta_x}$ factor), making the union bound over all $N_{\rm total}$ Freedman events polynomially small in $|D|$. Applying \cref{lem:Freedman} and summing the failure probabilities yields that, with probability at least $1 - |D|^{-\eta''}$, the Freedman inequality bounds hold simultaneously for all $\theta \in \mathcal{N}_{\rm net}$ and all algorithmic steps.
nodes.statement_short: Choice of z_Fr makes the union bound polynomially small
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Nearest net point decomposition
nodes.statement: We now extend to $\Theta_\circ$ via Lipschitz continuity. Working on the intersection of the activity event $E_{\rm act}$, and the window envelope event $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$, consider an arbitrary $\theta \in \Theta_\circ$. Let $\theta_g \in \mathcal{N}_{\rm net}$ be the closest net point, so $\|\theta - \theta_g\| \le \varepsilon_{\rm net}$. Let $X(\theta) = \int_D H(\tau; \theta) \mathrm{d} M^\star(\tau)$ be any of the generic martingale terms (e.g., from \cref{lem:perflip} or the gradient in Assumption \ref{ass:G7prime}). We decompose the value at $\theta$ as: \[ |X(\theta)| \le |X(\theta_g)| + |X(\theta) - X(\theta_g)|. \]
nodes.statement_short: Decompose X(theta) via the nearest net point
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Discretisation term
nodes.statement: The first term is bounded by the grid result in the above union bound. For the second term, we use the decomposition $\mathrm{d} M^\star = \mathrm{d} N - \lambda^\star \mathrm{d} \tau$: \[ |X(\theta) - X(\theta_g)| = \left| \int_D (H(\tau;\theta) - H(\tau;\theta_g)) \mathrm{d} M^\star \right| \le \int_D \Delta_H(\tau) \mathrm{d} N(\tau) + \int_D \Delta_H(\tau) \lambda^\star(\tau) \mathrm{d}\tau, \] where $\Delta_H(\tau) = |H(\tau;\theta) - H(\tau;\theta_g)|$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the second term via dN and lambda* dtau
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Lipschitz integrands
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:theta-Lip-integrands} (and the margins in Assumption~\ref{ass:G1}), the relevant integrands $H(\tau;\cdot)$ are Lipschitz in $\theta$ on $\Theta_\circ$ with a deterministic constant $L_H<\infty$ (dependent on model constants and $K_{\rm win}$, but independent of $|D|$). Thus $\Delta_H(\tau) \le L_H \varepsilon_{\rm net}$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrands are Lipschitz in theta
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Substitute
nodes.statement: Substituting this bound: \[ |X(\theta) - X(\theta_g)| \le L_H \varepsilon_{\rm net} \big( N(D) + \Lambda^\star(D) \big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Discretisation error bounded by L_H eps_net (N(D)+Lambda*(D))
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Negligible discretisation
nodes.statement: On $E_{\rm act}$ we have $N(D)=O(|D|)$, and on $\Omega_{n_*}$ we have $\Lambda^\star(D)=\int_D \lambda^\star \le K_{\rm win}|D|$. Since we chose $\varepsilon_{\rm net}=|D|^{-2}$, the discretization error is \[ O\!\left(L_H\,\varepsilon_{\rm net}\,(N(D)+\Lambda^\star(D))\right) =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\frac{L_H\,(1+K_{\rm win})}{|D|}\right). \] Since we chose $\varepsilon_{\rm net}=|D|^{-2}$, this discretization error is $O_{\mathbb P}\!\big(L_H(1+K_{\rm win})/|D|\big)$. When the corresponding term appears with the $|D|^{-1}$ normalization (as in $f_r=|D|^{-1}\ell_r$), the discretization contribution is $O_{\mathbb P}\!\big(L_H(1+K_{\rm win})/|D|^2\big)$, hence negligible.
nodes.statement_short: With eps_net=|D|^-2 the error is negligible
nodes.section: Penalized objective, per-flip bound, and E-step elimination

nodes.name: Flip differences and interpolation
nodes.statement: Fix two labellings $r,r'$ that differ at exactly one index $j$ (the ``flipped'' event), and write \[ \Delta\widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau):=\widehat\lambda_k^{r'}(\tau)-\widehat\lambda_k^{r}(\tau),\qquad \Delta\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau):=\widehat\lambda^{r'}(\tau)-\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau), \] where $\widehat\lambda^{r}=\widehat\lambda_0^{r}+\widehat\lambda_1^{r}$. For the remainder of this proof, we write $D:=D^{(m)}$ for brevity. For $v\in[0,1]$ also define the interpolated intensity \[ \widehat\lambda^{r,v}(\tau):=\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)+v\,\Delta\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau). \]
nodes.statement_short: Define intensity differences and the interpolated intensity

nodes.name: Total/selection split
nodes.statement: Using the decomposition \[ \sum_{k\in\{0,1\}}\int_D \log\widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau)\,dN_k^r(\tau) = \int_D \log\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)\,dN(\tau) + \sum_{k\in\{0,1\}}\int_D \log\!\Big(\frac{\widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau)}{\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)}\Big)\,dN_k^r(\tau), \] we may write the objective (restricted to $D$) as a sum of a total-intensity log-likelihood term and a selection term. Hence \[ \ell_{r'}^{[u_m]}(\theta)-\ell_r^{[u_m]}(\theta) = \Big[\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tot}}(r')-\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tot}}(r)\Big] + \Big[\mathcal L_{\mathrm{sel}}(r')-\mathcal L_{\mathrm{sel}}(r)\Big], \] where $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tot}}(r):=\int_D \log\widehat\lambda^{r}\,dN-\int_D \widehat\lambda^{r}\,d\tau$.
nodes.statement_short: Split the log-likelihood difference into total-intensity and selection parts

nodes.name: Log interpolation identity
nodes.statement: For the log term, apply the identity \[ \log a-\log b = (a-b)\int_0^1\frac{1}{b+v(a-b)}\,dv \qquad(a,b>0), \] pointwise with $a=\widehat\lambda^{r'}(\tau)$ and $b=\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)$ to obtain \[ \log\widehat\lambda^{r'}(\tau)-\log\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau) = \int_0^1 \frac{\Delta\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)}{\widehat\lambda^{r,v}(\tau)}\,dv. \] Therefore, \begin{align*} \mathcal L_{\mathrm{tot}}(r')-\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tot}}(r) &= \int_D\big(\log\widehat\lambda^{r'}-\log\widehat\lambda^{r}\big)\,dN - \int_D \Delta\widehat\lambda^{r}\,d\tau\\ &= \int_0^1\int_D \frac{\Delta\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)}{\widehat\lambda^{r,v}(\tau)}\,dN(\tau)\,dv - \int_D \Delta\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)\,d\tau. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Write log differences as v-integrals

nodes.name: Doob-Meyer split
nodes.statement: Now decompose $dN=dM^\star+\lambda^\star(\tau)\,d\tau$ to get \begin{align*} \mathcal L_{\mathrm{tot}}(r')-\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tot}}(r) &= \underbrace{\int_0^1\int_D \frac{\Delta\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)}{\widehat\lambda^{r,v}(\tau)}\,dM^\star(\tau)\,dv}_{:=\,\mathcal M_1} \\&\quad+ \int_0^1\int_D \frac{\Delta\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)}{\widehat\lambda^{r,v}(\tau)}\,\lambda^\star(\tau)\,d\tau\,dv - \int_D \Delta\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)\,d\tau\\ &= \mathcal M_1 + \int_0^1\int_D \frac{\Delta\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)}{\widehat\lambda^{r,v}(\tau)}\big(\lambda^\star(\tau)-\widehat\lambda^{r,v}(\tau)\big)\,d\tau\,dv. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Decompose dN to isolate the martingale M_1

nodes.name: Stochastic Fubini
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:stoch-fubini} (stochastic Fubini), we may interchange the $v$-integration and the martingale integral and write \[ \mathcal M_1=\int_D\left(\int_0^1 \frac{\Delta\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)}{\widehat\lambda^{r,v}(\tau)}\,dv\right)\,dM^\star(\tau), \] so $\mathcal M_1$ is a well-defined martingale integral.
nodes.statement_short: M_1 is a well-defined martingale integral

nodes.name: Drift terms D_1, D_2
nodes.statement: Using $\lambda^\star-\widehat\lambda^{r,v}=(\lambda^\star-\widehat\lambda^{r})-v\,\Delta\widehat\lambda^{r}$, the last integral becomes \begin{align*} &\int_0^1\int_D \frac{\Delta\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)\big(\lambda^\star(\tau)-\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)\big)}{\widehat\lambda^{r,v}(\tau)}\,d\tau\,dv - \int_0^1\int_D \frac{v\big(\Delta\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)\big)^2}{\widehat\lambda^{r,v}(\tau)}\,d\tau\,dv\\ &\qquad=: \mathcal D_1-\mathcal D_2. \end{align*} Thus $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tot}}(r')-\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tot}}(r)=\mathcal M_1+\mathcal D_1-\mathcal D_2$, matching the lemma's definitions. \medskip
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the remainder as D_1 - D_2

nodes.name: Selection term as event sum
nodes.statement: We now examine the selection part and the single-flip term. Write the selection term as an event-sum: \[ \mathcal L_{\mathrm{sel}}(r) = \sum_{k\in\{0,1\}}\int_D \log\!\Big(\frac{\widehat\lambda_k^{r}(\tau)}{\widehat\lambda^{r}(\tau)}\Big)\,dN_k^r(\tau) = \sum_{i:\,\gamma_i\in D} \log\!\Big(\frac{\widehat\lambda_{r_i}^{r}(\gamma_i)}{\widehat\lambda^{r}(\gamma_i)}\Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Write the selection term as a sum over events

nodes.name: Split at the flipped index
nodes.statement: Since $r$ and $r'$ differ only at $j$, split the difference into the contribution from $i\neq j$ and the contribution at index $j$: \begin{align*} \mathcal L_{\mathrm{sel}}(r')-\mathcal L_{\mathrm{sel}}(r) &= \sum_{\substack{i:\,\gamma_i\in D\\ i\neq j}} \Bigg[ \log\!\Big(\frac{\widehat\lambda_{r_i}^{r'}(\gamma_i)}{\widehat\lambda^{r'}(\gamma_i)}\Big) - \log\!\Big(\frac{\widehat\lambda_{r_i}^{r}(\gamma_i)}{\widehat\lambda^{r}(\gamma_i)}\Big) \Bigg]\\ &\quad+ \Bigg[ \log\!\Big(\frac{\widehat\lambda_{r'_{j}}^{r'}(\gamma_{j})}{\widehat\lambda^{r'}(\gamma_{j})}\Big) - \log\!\Big(\frac{\widehat\lambda_{r_{j}}^{r}(\gamma_{j})}{\widehat\lambda^{r}(\gamma_{j})}\Big) \Bigg]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Separate i != j from the flipped index j

nodes.name: Selection remainder
nodes.statement: By definition, the first sum is exactly the remainder term $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{sel}}$ in the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: The i != j sum is R_sel

nodes.name: Flipped-event term
nodes.statement: For the single flipped event, use predictability: at time $\gamma_{j}$, the pre-$t_j$ histories under $r$ and $r'$ coincide, so $\widehat\lambda_k^{r'}(\gamma_{j})=\widehat\lambda_k^{r}(\gamma_{j})$ for $k\in\{0,1\}$, and likewise $\widehat\lambda^{r'}(\gamma_{j})=\widehat\lambda^{r}(\gamma_{j})$. Therefore the bracket simplifies to \[ \log\!\Big(\frac{\widehat\lambda_{r'_j}^{\,r}(\gamma_j;\theta)}{\widehat\lambda_{r_j}^{\,r}(\gamma_j;\theta)}\Big) \;=\; \sigma_j\,\log\!\Big(\frac{\widehat\lambda_1^{\,r}(\gamma_j;\theta)}{\widehat\lambda_0^{\,r}(\gamma_j;\theta)}\Big) \;=\; \sigma_j\,\tilde s_\theta(\zeta;r), \] where $\sigma_j=+1$ for a $0\to1$ flip and $\sigma_j=-1$ for a $1\to0$ flip (as defined in the lemma), and $\tilde s_\theta(\zeta;r)$ is the log-ratio score at event $\zeta$.
nodes.statement_short: Predictability makes the flipped-event term sigma_j times the score

nodes.name: Per-flip identity
nodes.statement: Combining Step 1 and Step 2 yields the claimed per-flip identity.
nodes.statement_short: Combine total and selection parts

nodes.name: Drift bounds
nodes.statement: On the window envelope event $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$ from Assumption~\ref{ass:G2prime} (and hence on the master event of Lemma~\ref{lem:master}), the denominators in $\mathcal D_1,\mathcal D_2$ are bounded below by $\underline\mu_\Sigma$ by Assumption~\ref{ass:G1}, while the numerators are controlled by the single flip locality bounds in Assumption~\ref{ass:G3}. A direct computation gives \begin{align} |\mathcal D_1| &\le\frac{2B_1}{\underline\mu_\Sigma} K_{\rm win}, \notag\\ \mathcal D_2 &\le\frac{B_2}{2}. \notag \end{align} Therefore, on $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$ (and hence on the master event of Lemma~\ref{lem:master}), the drift terms satisfy \begin{align} |\mathcal D_1| \le \frac{2B_1}{\underline\mu_\Sigma} K_{\rm win},\qquad \mathcal D_2 \le \frac{B_2}{2}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Margins and locality bound D_1 and D_2 (eq. 20)

nodes.name: Domination of R_sel
nodes.statement: Using $| \log a-\log b|\le |a-b|/\min\{a,b\}$, Assumption~\ref{ass:G1}, and $|\Delta\widehat\lambda_{\mathrm{sel}_r}|\le |\Delta\widehat\lambda_0^r|+|\Delta\widehat\lambda_1^r|$ at event times, we have the pathwise domination \[ |\mathcal R_{\rm sel}| \ \le\ \int_D h(\tau)\,\mathrm{d} N(\tau), \qquad h(\tau):=\frac{|\Delta\widehat\lambda^r(\tau)|}{\underline\mu_\Sigma}+\frac{|\Delta\widehat\lambda_0^r(\tau)|+|\Delta\widehat\lambda_1^r(\tau)|}{\underline\mu_{\min}}. \] Since $h$ depends only on past labels through $\Delta\widehat\lambda_k^r$, it is $\mathcal G$-predictable under Assumption~\ref{ass:G0pred}. Decompose \[ \int_D h\,\mathrm{d} N=\underbrace{\int_D h\,\mathrm{d} M^\star}_{=:\ \mathcal M_{\rm sel}}+\underbrace{\int_D h(\tau)\lambda^\star(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau}_{=:\ \mathcal D_{\rm sel}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Dominate the selection remainder by an integral of a predictable h and split it

nodes.name: Selection drift and sup bound
nodes.statement: On $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$, $\|\lambda^\star\|_\infty\le K_{\rm win}$, hence \[ |\mathcal D_{\rm sel}| \ \le\ K_{\rm win}\int_D h \ \le\ \left(\frac{B_1}{\underline\mu_\Sigma}+\frac{B_1^\Sigma}{\underline\mu_{\min}}\right)K_{\rm win}. \] Moreover, $\|h\|_\infty\le H_{\rm sel}$ with \[ H_{\rm sel}:=\frac{B_\infty}{\underline\mu_\Sigma}+\frac{2B_\infty^{\rm comp}}{\underline\mu_{\min}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound D_sel and ||h||_inf

nodes.name: Freedman for martingale terms
nodes.statement: Applying \cref{lem:Freedman} to $\mathcal M_{\rm sel}$ gives \begin{align} |\mathcal M_1| &\le \sqrt{ \frac{2B_2}{\underline\mu_\Sigma} K_{\rm win} z_{\rm Fr}\ +\ \frac{B_\infty^2}{9\underline\mu_\Sigma^2} z_{\rm Fr}^2 }\ +\ \frac{B_\infty}{3\underline\mu_\Sigma} z_{\rm Fr} \ \le\ \sqrt{\frac{2B_2}{\underline\mu_\Sigma} K_{\rm win} z_{\rm Fr}}\ +\ \frac{2B_\infty}{3\underline\mu_\Sigma} z_{\rm Fr}, \end{align} where the final inequality uses $\sqrt{a+b}\le \sqrt a+\sqrt b$, producing an additional $(B_\infty/(3\underline\mu_\Sigma))z_{\rm Fr}$ term and hence the coefficient $2/3$ on the linear-in-$z_{\rm Fr}$ part. Similarly, \begin{align} |\mathcal M_{\rm sel}| &\le \sqrt{ 2K_{\rm win}\!\left(2\frac{B_2}{\underline\mu_\Sigma} + 4\frac{B_2^\Sigma\,\underline\mu_\Sigma}{\underline\mu_{\min}^2}\right) z_{\rm Fr}\ +\ \frac{H_{\rm sel}^2}{9}z_{\rm Fr}^2 }\ +\ \frac{H_{\rm sel}}{3}z_{\rm Fr}\notag\\ &\le 2\sqrt{\left(\frac{B_2}{\underline\mu_\Sigma} + 2\frac{B_2^\Sigma\,\underline\mu_\Sigma}{\underline\mu_{\min}^2}\right)K_{\rm win} z_{\rm Fr}}\ +\ \frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{B_\infty}{\underline\mu_\Sigma} + \frac{2B_\infty^{\rm comp}}{\underline\mu_{\min}}\right)z_{\rm Fr}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Freedman bounds for M_1 and M_sel (eqs. 21-22)

nodes.name: Uniform per-flip bound
nodes.statement: Consequently, setting \[ C_{\rm dr,0}:=\frac{B_2}{2},\qquad C_{\rm dr,1}:=\frac{3B_1}{\underline\mu_\Sigma}+\frac{B_1^{\Sigma}}{\underline\mu_{\min}}, \] and \[ C_{\rm mtg,1}:=\sqrt{\frac{2B_2}{\underline\mu_\Sigma}} + 2\sqrt{\frac{B_2}{\underline\mu_\Sigma}+2\frac{B_2^{\Sigma}\,\underline\mu_\Sigma}{\underline\mu_{\min}^2}},\qquad C_{\rm mtg,2}:=\frac{4}{3}\!\left(\frac{B_\infty}{\underline\mu_\Sigma}+\frac{B_\infty^{\rm comp}}{\underline\mu_{\min}}\right), \] we have the uniform per-flip bound \begin{equation} \Big|\ell_{r'}^{[u_m]}(\theta)-\ell_r^{[u_m]}(\theta)-\sigma_j\,\tilde s_\theta(\zeta;r)\Big| \ \le\ C_{\rm dr,0}\ +\ C_{\rm dr,1} K_{\rm win}\ +\ C_{\rm mtg,1}\sqrt{K_{\rm win} z_{\rm Fr}}\ +\ C_{\rm mtg,2} z_{\rm Fr}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Collect constants into the per-flip bound (eq. 23)

nodes.name: Minority-creating flip
nodes.statement: Hence, if the flip at $\zeta\in S_\theta^\pm(b)$ creates a minority, then \[ \mathcal J_\alpha^{[u_m]}(r',\theta)-\mathcal J_\alpha^{[u_m]}(r,\theta)\ \le\ (C_{\rm dr,1}-\alpha) K_{\rm win}\ +\ \Big(C_{\rm dr,0}+C_{\rm mtg,1}\sqrt{K_{\rm win}z_{\rm Fr}}+C_{\rm mtg,2}z_{\rm Fr}-(b-\Delta_s)\Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Penalised objective drops when a flip creates a minority

nodes.name: Minority-eliminating flip
nodes.statement: On \(E^{\rm align}_{|D|}\), Assumption~\ref{ass:G4} implies that for \(\zeta\in S_\theta^+(b)\) we have \(\tilde s_\theta(\zeta;r)\ge b-\Delta_s\), and for \(\zeta\in S_\theta^-(b)\) we have \(\tilde s_\theta(\zeta;r)\le -b+\Delta_s\).If it eliminates a minority, then \[ \mathcal J_\alpha^{[u_m]}(r',\theta)-\mathcal J_\alpha^{[u_m]}(r,\theta)\ \ge\ (\alpha-C_{\rm dr,1}) K_{\rm win}\ -\ \big(C_{\rm dr,0}+C_{\rm mtg,1}\sqrt{K_{\rm win}z_{\rm Fr}}+C_{\rm mtg,2}z_{\rm Fr}\big)\ +\ (b-\Delta_s). \]
nodes.statement_short: Alignment bounds the score; eliminating a minority increases the objective

nodes.name: Sufficient condition
nodes.statement: Therefore the following sufficient condition ensures elimination and non-creation of minorities on $S_\theta^\pm(b)$: \begin{align} &(\alpha-C_{\rm dr,1}) K_{\rm win}\ \ge\ C_{\rm mtg,1}\sqrt{K_{\rm win}z_{\rm Fr}}+C_{\rm mtg,2}z_{\rm Fr}+\kappa_b,\qquad b \ge \Delta_s + C_{\rm dr,0} - \kappa_b, \end{align} for some \(\kappa_b\in[0,C_{\rm dr,0}]\), where \(\Delta_s=\Delta_s(|D|)\) is the alignment slack from Assumption~\ref{ass:G4}, written in shorthand on \(E^{\rm align}_{|D|}\); it is independent of \(b\). Note that the greedy scan \eqref{eq:greedy-estep} eliminates minorities on decisive sets under the weaker condition \(b+\alpha K_{\rm win}\ge \Delta_s\) (Lemma~\ref{lem:E-elim}); \eqref{eq:EsufficientB} is tailored to per-flip comparisons of \(\mathcal J_\alpha^{[u_m]}\) that control future effects.
nodes.statement_short: Derive the sufficient condition (eq. 24)

nodes.name: Case S^+
nodes.statement: Fix an event index $i$ with $u_m<t_i\le u_{m+1}$ and $\gamma_i\in S^+_{\theta^{(m)}}(b)$. The minority label is $0$, hence the greedy score difference between choosing $1$ and choosing $0$ equals \[ \Big(\log \widehat\lambda_{1}^{r^{(m+1)}}(\gamma_i;\theta^{(m)})\Big) -\Big(\log \widehat\lambda_{0}^{r^{(m+1)}}(\gamma_i;\theta^{(m)})-\alpha K_{\rm win}\Big) =\tilde s_{\theta^{(m)}}(\gamma_i;r^{(m+1)})+\alpha K_{\rm win}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Compute the greedy score difference on S^+

nodes.name: Alignment bound on S^+
nodes.statement: By Assumption~\ref{ass:G4}, $\tilde s_{\theta^{(m)}}(\gamma_i;r^{(m+1)})\ge b-\Delta_s$, hence \[ \tilde s_{\theta^{(m)}}(\gamma_i;r^{(m+1)})+\alpha K_{\rm win}\ \ge\ b-\Delta_s+\alpha K_{\rm win}\ \ge\ 0 \] by \eqref{eq:Eelim-cond}. Therefore the non-minority label is chosen (ties broken toward the non-minority label).
nodes.statement_short: Alignment and the condition make the difference nonnegative

nodes.name: Case S^-
nodes.statement: If $\gamma_i\in S^-_{\theta^{(m)}}(b)$ then $\tilde s_{\theta^{(m)}}(\gamma_i;r^{(m+1)})\le -b+\Delta_s$, so \[ (-\tilde s_{\theta^{(m)}}(\gamma_i;r^{(m+1)}))+\alpha K_{\rm win} \ \ge\ b-\Delta_s+\alpha K_{\rm win}\ \ge\ 0, \] and the greedy rule chooses label $0$ (ties broken toward the non-minority label).
nodes.statement_short: Symmetric argument on S^-

nodes.name: No minorities
nodes.statement: Hence no minorities are assigned on $S^+_{\theta^{(m)}}(b)\cup S^-_{\theta^{(m)}}(b)$ within the processed block.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude for the whole processed block

nodes.name: Pointwise inclusion
nodes.statement: Let $\Delta_{\rm LLR}:=s_{\theta^\star}^{\rm or}-s_{\theta^{(m)}}^{\rm or}$. The symmetric-difference inclusions yield the pointwise bound on $D$: \[ \mathbbm{1}_{B_{\theta^{(m)}}} \ \le\ \mathbbm{1}_{A_{\theta^\star}(2b)} + \mathbbm{1}_{\{|\Delta_{\rm LLR}|\ge b\}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Disagreement set lies in the 2b-band plus a large-LLR-change set
nodes.section: Decisive-set stability and E-step Hamming bound

nodes.name: Integrated inclusion
nodes.statement: Intersect with $W$ and multiply by $\lambda^\star$ to obtain \[ \int_{B_{\theta^{(m)}}\cap W}\lambda^\star(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau \ \le\ \int_{A_{\theta^\star}(2b)\cap W}\lambda^\star(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau \ +\ \frac{1}{b}\int_W |\Delta_{\rm LLR}(\tau)|\,\lambda^\star(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau. \]
nodes.statement_short: Integrate against lambda* with Markov on the LLR change
nodes.section: Decisive-set stability and E-step Hamming bound

nodes.name: LLR Lipschitz
nodes.statement: On $E^{\rm Lip}_{|D|}$, Assumption~\ref{ass:G5} (applied to the subwindow $W$) gives \[ \int_W |\Delta_{\rm LLR}(\tau)|\,\lambda^\star(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau \ \le\ L_s\,|W|\,\|\theta^{(m)}-\theta^\star\|. \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound the LLR change by L_s |W| ||theta - theta*||
nodes.section: Decisive-set stability and E-step Hamming bound

nodes.name: Compensator deviations
nodes.statement: On $E^{\rm mass}_{|D|}$ (strengthened to include the restricted sets) we have the compensator deviations \[ N(B_{\theta^{(m)}}\cap W)\ \le\ \int_{B_{\theta^{(m)}}\cap W}\lambda^\star(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau\ +\ C_{\rm it}\sqrt{K_{\rm win}|W|\log|D|}, \] \[ N(A_{\theta^\star}(2b)\cap W)\ \ge\ \int_{A_{\theta^\star}(2b)\cap W}\lambda^\star(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau\ -\ C_{\rm it}\sqrt{K_{\rm win}|W|\log|D|}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Pass from compensators to counts
nodes.section: Decisive-set stability and E-step Hamming bound

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combine the last three displays to conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the displays
nodes.section: Decisive-set stability and E-step Hamming bound

nodes.name: Work on master event
nodes.statement: Work on the master event of \cref{lem:master}, so in particular on $E^{\rm Lip}_{|D|}\cap E^{\rm mass}_{|D|}$ (with the deterministic subwindow restrictions included as in Assumption~\ref{ass:G8}), and assume \cref{lem:E-elim} applies to the greedy E-step on the processed block $D_{m+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Work on the master event with E-step elimination
nodes.section: Decisive-set stability and E-step Hamming bound

nodes.name: Increment on new block only
nodes.statement: By Assumption~\ref{ass:G0pred}(b), labels are not revised: $r^{(m+1)}_i=r^{(m)}_i$ for all $i$ with $t_i\le u_m$. Hence $\Delta_{m+1}$ counts disagreements between $r^{(m+1)}$ and $r^\star$ only among events in $D_{m+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Delta_{m+1} counts disagreements only in D_{m+1}
nodes.section: Decisive-set stability and E-step Hamming bound

nodes.name: Regions R_1-R_4
nodes.statement: Define the sets (as subsets of $D$) \[ R_1:=S_{\theta^{(m)}}^+(b)\cap S_{\theta^\star}^+(b),\quad R_2:=S_{\theta^{(m)}}^-(b)\cap S_{\theta^\star}^-(b),\quad R_3:=B_{\theta^{(m)}},\quad R_4:=A_{\theta^\star}(b). \]
nodes.statement_short: Define the four regions
nodes.section: Decisive-set stability and E-step Hamming bound

nodes.name: Locate disagreements
nodes.statement: By \cref{lem:E-elim}, within $D_{m+1}$ all decisive-set labels match the non-minority choice at $\theta^{(m)}$. Therefore any disagreement within $D_{m+1}$ must occur either as an oracle minority on $R_1$/$R_2$, or in $B_{\theta^{(m)}}$, or in the ambiguous band $A_{\theta^\star}(b)$, hence \[ \Delta_{m+1} \ \le\ N_0(R_1\cap D_{m+1})+N_1(R_2\cap D_{m+1})+N(R_3\cap D_{m+1})+N(R_4\cap D_{m+1}). \]
nodes.statement_short: Disagreements occur only as oracle minorities, in B_theta or in the band
nodes.section: Decisive-set stability and E-step Hamming bound

nodes.name: Enlarge to oracle sets
nodes.statement: Since $R_1\subseteq S_{\theta^\star}^+(b)$ and $R_2\subseteq S_{\theta^\star}^-(b)$, \[ N_0(R_1\cap D_{m+1})\le N_0\!\big(S_{\theta^\star}^+(b)\cap D_{m+1}\big),\qquad N_1(R_2\cap D_{m+1})\le N_1\!\big(S_{\theta^\star}^-(b)\cap D_{m+1}\big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Enlarge regions to oracle decisive sets
nodes.section: Decisive-set stability and E-step Hamming bound

nodes.name: Enlarge band and disagreement
nodes.statement: Also $R_3\cap D_{m+1}\subseteq B_{\theta^{(m)}}\cap D_{m+1}$ and $R_4\cap D_{m+1}\subseteq A_{\theta^\star}(2b)\cap D_{m+1}$, hence \[ N(R_3\cap D_{m+1})\le N(B_{\theta^{(m)}}\cap D_{m+1}),\qquad N(R_4\cap D_{m+1})\le N\!\big(A_{\theta^\star}(2b)\cap D_{m+1}\big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Enlarge R_3 and R_4
nodes.section: Decisive-set stability and E-step Hamming bound

nodes.name: Oracle-minority mass
nodes.statement: Bound the oracle-minority terms using Assumption~\ref{ass:G8} applied on the block window $D_{m+1}$ and the corresponding mean deviations included in $E^{\rm mass}_{|D|}$: \[ \frac{N_0(S_{\theta^\star}^+(b)\cap D_{m+1})+N_1(S_{\theta^\star}^-(b)\cap D_{m+1})}{|D_{m+1}|} \ \le\ \eta_+(|D_{m+1}|;b)+\eta_-(|D_{m+1}|;b)\ +\ 4C_{\rm it}\sqrt{\frac{K_{\rm win}\log|D|}{|D_{m+1}|}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Assumption 18 bounds the minority mass
nodes.section: Decisive-set stability and E-step Hamming bound

nodes.name: Decisive-set stability
nodes.statement: For the $B_{\theta^{(m)}}$ term, apply Lemma~\ref{lem:set-stab} with $W=D_{m+1}$ and divide by $|D_{m+1}|$: \[ \frac{N(B_{\theta^{(m)}}\cap D_{m+1})}{|D_{m+1}|} \ \le\ \frac{L_s}{b}\,\|\theta^{(m)}-\theta^\star\| \ +\ \frac{1}{|D_{m+1}|}N\!\big(A_{\theta^\star}(2b)\cap D_{m+1}\big) \ +\ 2C_{\rm it}\sqrt{\frac{K_{\rm win}\log|D|}{|D_{m+1}|}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 14 on the block
nodes.section: Decisive-set stability and E-step Hamming bound

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combine the last three displays and use $\log|D|\le z_{\rm Fr}$ for all large $|D|$ to obtain the stated bound with $\delta_m=C_{\rm H,1}\sqrt{K_{\rm win}z_{\rm Fr}/|D_{m+1}|}$ and $C_{\rm H,1}=6C_{\rm it}$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine and use log|D| <= z_Fr
nodes.section: Decisive-set stability and E-step Hamming bound

nodes.name: Strong monotonicity of -f
nodes.statement: Strong concavity of $f$ is equivalent to $m_{\rm sc}$--strong convexity of $-f$. Hence for all $\theta,\theta'\in\Theta$, \[ \big(\nabla(-f)(\theta')-\nabla(-f)(\theta)\big)^\top(\theta'-\theta)\ \ge\ m_{\rm sc}\|\theta'-\theta\|^2. \]
nodes.statement_short: Strong convexity of -f gives gradient monotonicity
nodes.section: M-step bound via tightened label-to-score Lipschitz

nodes.name: Sign flip
nodes.statement: Multiplying by $-1$ gives the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Multiply by -1
nodes.section: M-step bound via tightened label-to-score Lipschitz

nodes.name: Strong concavity at the maximiser
nodes.statement: Let $u:=u_{m+1}$ and write $\hat\theta:=\hat\theta_r^{[u]}$ for brevity. Since $\hat\theta,\theta^\star\in\Theta_{\rm sc}$ and (on the master event) $f_{r^\star}^{[u]}$ is $m_{\rm sc}$--strongly concave on $\Theta_{\rm sc}$ (Assumption~\ref{ass:G6}, applied to the restricted objective on $D^{[u]}$), apply \cref{lem:sc-mon} on $\Theta=\Theta_{\rm sc}$ with $f=f_{r^\star}^{[u]}$, $\theta=\theta^\star$ and $\theta'=\hat\theta$ to get \[ -m_{\rm sc}\|\hat\theta-\theta^\star\|^2\ \ge\ \big(\nabla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(\hat\theta)-\nabla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(\theta^\star)\big)^\top(\hat\theta-\theta^\star). \]
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 15 to f_{r*} on Theta_sc
nodes.section: M-step bound via tightened label-to-score Lipschitz

nodes.name: Rearrange
nodes.statement: Rearranging, \[ m_{\rm sc}\|\hat\theta-\theta^\star\|^2\ \le\ \big(\nabla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(\theta^\star)-\nabla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(\hat\theta)\big)^\top(\hat\theta-\theta^\star). \]
nodes.statement_short: Rearrange the inequality
nodes.section: M-step bound via tightened label-to-score Lipschitz

nodes.name: Insert gradient of f_r
nodes.statement:
Insert and subtract $
abla f_r^{[u]}(\hat	heta)$:  egin{align*} m_{m sc}\|\hat	heta-	heta^\star\|^2 &\le  ig(
abla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(	heta^\star)-
abla f_r^{[u]}(\hat	heta) ig)^	op(\hat	heta-	heta^\star) +  ig(
abla f_r^{[u]}(\hat	heta)-
abla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(\hat	heta) ig)^	op(\hat	heta-	heta^\star). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Insert and subtract grad f_r at the maximiser
nodes.section: M-step bound via tightened label-to-score Lipschitz

nodes.name: First-order condition
nodes.statement:
By Assumption~ef{ass:G9} applied to the restricted objective $f_r^{[u]}$ with $	heta=	heta^\star$, we have $(	heta^\star-\hat	heta)^	op 
abla f_r^{[u]}(\hat	heta)\le 0$, i.e.\ $(\hat	heta-	heta^\star)^	op 
abla f_r^{[u]}(\hat	heta)\ge 0$. Hence \[  ig(
abla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(	heta^\star)-
abla f_r^{[u]}(\hat	heta) ig)^	op(\hat	heta-	heta^\star) \le 
abla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(	heta^\star)^	op(\hat	heta-	heta^\star) \le \|
abla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(	heta^\star)\|\,\|\hat	heta-	heta^\star\|. \]
nodes.statement_short: Variational inequality bounds the first term
nodes.section: M-step bound via tightened label-to-score Lipschitz

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement:
Also, \[  ig(
abla f_r^{[u]}(\hat	heta)-
abla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(\hat	heta) ig)^	op(\hat	heta-	heta^\star) \le \|
abla f_r^{[u]}(\hat	heta)-
abla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(\hat	heta)\|\,\|\hat	heta-	heta^\star\|. \]
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz on the second term
nodes.section: M-step bound via tightened label-to-score Lipschitz

nodes.name: Divide
nodes.statement:
Dividing by $m_{m sc}\|\hat	heta-	heta^\star\|$ (or arguing trivially if $\hat	heta=	heta^\star$) yields \[ m_{m sc}\|\hat	heta-	heta^\star\| \le \|
abla f_r^{[u]}(\hat	heta)-
abla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(\hat	heta)\| + \|
abla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(	heta^\star)\|. \]
nodes.statement_short: Divide to get a linear bound
nodes.section: M-step bound via tightened label-to-score Lipschitz

nodes.name: Label-to-score and score bounds
nodes.statement:
On the master event, the first norm is bounded by Assumption~ef{ass:G7prime}, and the second by Assumption~ef{ass:G6}(b) (applied on the prefix window $D^{[u]}$): \[ \|
abla f_r^{[u]}(\hat	heta)-
abla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(\hat	heta)\| \ \le\  rac{d_H^{[u]}(r,r^\star)}{|D^{[u]}|}\Big( ar C_0 K_{m win} +  ar C_1\sqrt{K_{m win} z_{m Fr}} +  ar C_2 z_{m Fr}\Big), \] \[ \|
abla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(	heta^\star)\| \ \le\ C_{m sc}\!\left(\sqrt{ rac{K_{m win} z_{m Fr}}{|D^{[u]}|}} +  rac{z_{m Fr}}{|D^{[u]}|}ight). \]
nodes.statement_short: Apply Assumptions 17 and 15(b)
nodes.section: M-step bound via tightened label-to-score Lipschitz

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Divide by $m_{\rm sc}$ and note $|D^{[u]}|=|D^{(m+1)}|$.
nodes.statement_short: Divide by m_sc
nodes.section: M-step bound via tightened label-to-score Lipschitz

nodes.name: Base case
nodes.statement: By induction. The base case is $\|\theta^{(0)}-\theta^\star\|\le r_{\rm sc}$.
nodes.statement_short: Base case from the warm start
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Inductive step
nodes.statement: If $\|\theta^{(m)}-\theta^\star\|\le r_{\rm sc}$ then \[ \|\theta^{(m+1)}-\theta^\star\| \le \rho\,r_{\rm sc}+s \le \rho\,r_{\rm sc}+(1-\rho)\,r_{\rm sc} = r_{\rm sc}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Contraction keeps the next iterate within r_sc
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Additivity of Hamming counts
nodes.statement: Since labels are not revised (Assumption~\ref{ass:G0pred}(b)), we have $d_H^{[u_{m+1}]}=d_H^{[u_m]}+\Delta_{m+1}$ for every $m$.
nodes.statement_short: Non-revision gives additive prefix Hamming counts
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Normalise
nodes.statement_short: Divide by the prefix volume
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Case m >= 1
nodes.statement: For $m\ge 1$ this is exactly the claimed identity with $e_m=d_H^{[u_m]}/|D^{(m)}|$.
nodes.statement_short: Read off the identity
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Case m = 0
nodes.statement: For $m=0$ the same formula holds by the convention $e_0:=0$ and $\omega_0=|D^{(0)}|/|D^{(1)}|=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Convention e_0 = 0 and omega_0 = 0
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Bound outside Theta_loc
nodes.statement: Fix $\theta\in\Theta_\circ\setminus\Theta_{\rm loc}$. On $E_{\rm gap}^{[u]}$, \[ f_r^{[u]}(\theta)\ \le\ f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(\theta)+\frac{\Delta_{\rm gap}}{4} \ \le\ f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(\theta^\star)-\Delta_{\rm gap}+\frac{\Delta_{\rm gap}}{4} \ =\ f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(\theta^\star)-\frac{3}{4}\Delta_{\rm gap}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Gap plus perturbation bound outside Theta_loc
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Bound at theta*
nodes.statement: Also on $E_{\rm gap}^{[u]}$, \[ f_r^{[u]}(\theta^\star)\ \ge\ f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(\theta^\star)-\frac{\Delta_{\rm gap}}{4}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Perturbation bound at theta*
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: No maximiser outside
nodes.statement: Therefore \[ f_r^{[u]}(\theta)\ \le\ f_r^{[u]}(\theta^\star)-\frac{\Delta_{\rm gap}}{2}, \] so no maximiser of $f_r^{[u]}$ over $\Theta_\circ$ can lie in $\Theta_\circ\setminus\Theta_{\rm loc}$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine: values outside are Delta_gap/2 below
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Maximiser sets coincide
nodes.statement: Since $\Theta_{\rm loc}\subseteq\Theta_\circ$, the maximiser sets over $\Theta_\circ$ and $\Theta_{\rm loc}$ coincide.
nodes.statement_short: Hence the argmax sets coincide
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Set-up
nodes.statement: Work on the stated high-probability event. Fix $m\in\{0,\dots,\mathfrak{T}-1\}$. The quantity $\Delta_{m+1}$ counts mislabels in the block $D_{m+1}$ produced by the greedy rule \eqref{eq:greedy-estep} at parameter $\theta^{(m)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a block and the greedy update
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Block bound and averaging
nodes.statement: Proposition~\ref{prop:Estep} gives \eqref{eq:block-mislabel-rate} directly (with $\varepsilon_{m+1}=\Delta_{m+1}/|D_{m+1}|$). Identity \eqref{eq:prefix-avg-rec} is exactly Lemma~\ref{lem:avg-hamming} written in terms of $(e_m)$ and $(\varepsilon_{m+1})$.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 5 and Lemma 17 give the block and averaging bounds
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{eq:prefix-avg-rec} with \eqref{eq:block-mislabel-rate} gives \[ e_{m+1}\ \le\ \omega_m e_m+(1-\omega_m)\Big(A\|\theta^{(m)}-\theta^\star\|+\varepsilon_{b,m}+\delta_m\Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Combine averaging and block bounds
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Insert M-step bound
nodes.statement: For $m\ge 1$, apply Proposition~\ref{prop:Mstep} at index $m-1$ to bound $\|\theta^{(m)}-\theta^\star\|\le B_{\rm main}e_m+\xi_m$, yielding \eqref{eq:e-recursion}.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 6 closes the recursion
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Iterate recursion
nodes.statement: Equation \eqref{eq:theta-from-e} is exactly Proposition~\ref{prop:Mstep} rewritten with $e_{m+1}=d_H^{[u_{m+1}]}/|D^{(m+1)}|$. Finally, if $\rho<1$, iterating \eqref{eq:e-recursion} (with $\rho_m\le\rho$) gives the displayed geometric bound on $e_m$, and plugging into \eqref{eq:theta-from-e} yields the bound on $\|\theta^{(m)}-\theta^\star\|$.
nodes.statement_short: Iterate the recursion for geometric bounds
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Consistency
nodes.statement: The final consistency statement follows by combining the displayed bound on \(e_m\) with \eqref{eq:theta-from-e}: under \[ B_{\rm main}\,\rho^{\mathfrak{T}-1} e_1 \xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0,\qquad B_{\rm main}\,\frac{\max_{1\le j\le \mathfrak{T}-1}\big(A\,\xi_j+\varepsilon_{b,j}+\delta_j\big)}{1-\rho}\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0,\qquad \xi_{\mathfrak{T}}\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0, \] we obtain \(\|\theta^{(\mathfrak{T})}-\theta^\star\|\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0\).
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing terms give consistency
nodes.section: Two-line recursion and contraction to a statistical floor

nodes.name: Bracketing
nodes.statement: Under \cref{ass:CSC} and the bounds $a_{\rm csc}u_k U\le \sum_\ell (g_{k\ell}*N_\ell)\le b_{\rm csc}u_k U$, we obtain \[ \log\left(\frac{\mu_1+a_{\rm csc}u_1 U}{\mu_0+b_{\rm csc}u_0 U}\right)\ \le\ s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}\ \le\ \log\left(\frac{\mu_1+b_{\rm csc}u_1 U}{\mu_0+a_{\rm csc}u_0 U}\right). \]
nodes.statement_short: CSC brackets the oracle log-odds
nodes.section: When does the floor vanish? Parameter regimes

nodes.name: Deviation from baseline log-odds
nodes.statement: Write $s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}-S_0=\log(1+\delta_1)-\log(1+\delta_0)$ with \( \delta_1=\frac{c_1u_1U}{\mu_1},\ \delta_0=\frac{c_0u_0U}{\mu_0}, \) where $c_1,c_0\in[a_{\rm csc},b_{\rm csc}]$ and $\delta_0,\delta_1\ge0$. Using $\log(1+u)\le u$ for $u\ge0$, \[ \big|s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}-S_0\big| \ \le\ \log(1+\delta_1)+\log(1+\delta_0) \ \le\ \delta_1+\delta_0 \ \le\ \left(\frac{b_{\rm csc}u_1}{\mu_1}+\frac{b_{\rm csc}u_0}{\mu_0}\right)U. \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound |s^or - S_0| by delta_1 + delta_0
nodes.section: When does the floor vanish? Parameter regimes

nodes.name: Kappa bound
nodes.statement: Since $\mu_k\ge \underline\mu_k$, $U\le \kappa \mu_\Sigma^{\rm base}(\tau)$, and $\mu_\Sigma^{\rm base}(\tau)\le \sup_\tau \mu_\Sigma^{\rm base}(\tau)$, we get \[ \big|s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}-S_0\big|\ \le\ C_A' \kappa. \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound the deviation by C'_A kappa
nodes.section: When does the floor vanish? Parameter regimes

nodes.name: Band inclusion
nodes.statement: Therefore, \[ \{ |s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}|\le 2b \}\ \subseteq\ \{ |S_0|\le 2b+C_A'\kappa \}. \]
nodes.statement_short: The 2b-band lies in a widened baseline band
nodes.section: When does the floor vanish? Parameter regimes

nodes.name: Integrate density bound
nodes.statement: Multiplying by $\lambda^\star$, integrating, and dividing by $|D|$ yields \begin{align*} C_b(\theta^\star) &\le \frac{1}{|D|}\int_D \mathbbm{1}\{|S_0(\tau)|\le 2b+C_A'\kappa\}\,\lambda^\star(\tau)\,\mathrm{d}\tau \\ &= \frac{\Lambda^\star(D)}{|D|}\, \mathbb P_{\lambda^\star}\!\big(|S_0(\tau)|\le 2b+C_A'\kappa\big) \ \le\ 2L_0\,(2b+C_A'\kappa)\,\frac{\Lambda^\star(D)}{|D|}, \end{align*} whenever $2b+C_A'\kappa\le \epsilon_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate and use the density bound
nodes.section: When does the floor vanish? Parameter regimes

nodes.name: Lower bracket function
nodes.statement: For any $\tau$, define $\phi_{\rm low}(S):=\log\frac{\mu_1(\tau;\theta^\star)+a_{\rm csc}u_1 S}{\mu_0(\tau;\theta^\star)+b_{\rm csc}u_0 S}$ for $S\ge 0$. Its derivative is \[ \phi_{\rm low}'(S)\ =\ \frac{a_{\rm csc}u_1 \mu_0\ -\ b_{\rm csc}u_0 \mu_1}{(\mu_1+a_{\rm csc}u_1 S)(\mu_0+b_{\rm csc}u_0 S)}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Define phi_low and compute its derivative
nodes.section: When does the floor vanish? Parameter regimes

nodes.name: Monotonicity
nodes.statement: The dominant-bias condition $C_\mu < (u_1/u_0)/q$ implies $\frac{\mu_1}{\mu_0} < \frac{a_{\rm csc} u_1}{b_{\rm csc} u_0}$, so the numerator $a_{\rm csc} u_1 \mu_0 - b_{\rm csc} u_0 \mu_1$ is strictly positive. Thus $\phi_{\rm low}$ is strictly increasing in $S\ge 0$, with $\phi_{\rm low}(0)=S_0(\tau)$ and $\lim_{S\to\infty}\phi_{\rm low}(S)=\log(a_{\rm csc}u_1/b_{\rm csc}u_0)=\Delta_{\rm bias}$.
nodes.statement_short: Dominant bias makes phi_low increasing
nodes.section: When does the floor vanish? Parameter regimes

nodes.name: s^or >= S_0 >= 0
nodes.statement: By the bracketing inequality from \cref{lem:regA}, we have $s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}(\tau)\ge \phi_{\rm low}(U(\tau))$. Since $\phi_{\rm low}$ is increasing, $\phi_{\rm low}(U)\ge \phi_{\rm low}(0)=S_0(\tau)$. Under the alignment assumption, $S_0(\tau)\ge 0$, hence \[ s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}(\tau)\ \ge\ S_0(\tau)\ \ge\ 0, \] so $|s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}(\tau)| = s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}(\tau)$.
nodes.statement_short: Bracketing and alignment give s^or >= S_0 >= 0
nodes.section: When does the floor vanish? Parameter regimes

nodes.name: Inclusion
nodes.statement: Therefore, if $|s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}(\tau)|\le 2b$ then \[ 0\ \le\ S_0(\tau)\ \le\ s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}(\tau)\ \le\ 2b, \] which implies $|S_0(\tau)|\le 2b$. This proves the inclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Deduce the inclusion
nodes.section: When does the floor vanish? Parameter regimes

nodes.name: Band mass bound
nodes.statement: The bound on $C_b(\theta^\star)$ follows by integrating $\mathbbm{1}\{|S_0|\le 2b\}$ against $\lambda^\star$ and using the density bound.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the density bound
nodes.section: When does the floor vanish? Parameter regimes

nodes.name: Lipschitz functional
nodes.statement: By linearity and \eqref{eq:Lambda-Lip}, $|F(\theta)-F(\theta')|\le L_\lambda(\sum_\ell |c_\ell||B_\ell|)\|\theta-\theta'\|$.
nodes.statement_short: Linearity plus the Lipschitz envelope

nodes.name: Plug in iterate
nodes.statement: Apply this with $\theta=\theta^{(m)}$ and $\theta'=\theta^\star$.
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate at theta^(m) and theta*

nodes.name: Use M-step bound
nodes.statement: The bounds in terms of $(e_m)$ and $(\xi_m)$ follow directly from \eqref{eq:theta-from-e} in \cref{thm:contract}.
nodes.statement_short: Insert Theorem 13.1's bound

nodes.name: Cluster representation
nodes.statement: Because $g_{k\ell}\ge 0$ and $\xi(A)<1$, the multivariate Hawkes process admits the standard Poisson cluster (branching) representation on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathcal S$ (see, e.g., the stability/cluster constructions used already in Proposition~\ref{prop:hawkes-tail}). In this representation, events arise from immigrants generated by an inhomogeneous Poisson process with intensity $\mu_k(\tau;\theta^\star)$ for each mark $k$, and offspring generated recursively, wherein a parent of mark $\ell$ produces children of mark $k$ according to an inhomogeneous Poisson process with intensity kernel $g_{k\ell}$ shifted to the parent location.
nodes.statement_short: Use the Poisson cluster representation

nodes.name: Immigrant count
nodes.statement: Let $N^{\rm imm}(D)$ denote the number of immigrants in $D$ (all marks). Since $\mu_0(\tau;\theta^\star)+\mu_1(\tau;\theta^\star)\le \overline\mu_0+\overline\mu_1=:M_\Sigma^{\rm base}$ pointwise, \[ N^{\rm imm}(D)\ \preceq\ \mathrm{Pois}(M_\Sigma^{\rm base}\,|D|), \qquad \mathbb{E} N^{\rm imm}(D)\ \le\ M_\Sigma^{\rm base}\,|D|. \]
nodes.statement_short: Immigrants are dominated by a Poisson count

nodes.name: Progeny sizes
nodes.statement: For $k\in\{0,1\}$, let $Z^{(k)}$ be the total progeny size (all marks, including the ancestor) of a cluster started by a single immigrant of mark $k$, in the unrestricted process (no truncation by $D$). Under $\xi(A)<1$ and compactly supported kernels, $(Z^{(k)})$ has finite mean and admits a nontrivial exponential moment: there exists $\theta_0>0$ such that \[ m_1\ :=\ \max_{k\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb{E} Z^{(k)}\ <\ \infty, \qquad m_\theta\ :=\ \max_{k\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb{E}\big[e^{\theta Z^{(k)}}\big]\ <\ \infty \quad\text{for all }\theta\in(0,\theta_0]. \] (Heuristically: the offspring counts are Poisson with means $A_{k\ell}$, and subcriticality implies the associated multitype Galton--Watson total population has a finite exponential moment for small $\theta>0$.)
nodes.statement_short: Total progeny has finite mean and exponential moment

nodes.name: Compound domination
nodes.statement: Now dominate $N(D)$ by the total number of points generated by immigrants in $D$: if $(Z_i)$ are i.i.d.\ copies of a random variable $Z$ satisfying $Z\overset{d}{\ge} Z^{(k)}$ for both $k$ (e.g.\ take $Z$ to be a mixture maximising the mgf), then \[ N(D)\ \le\ \sum_{i=1}^{N^{\rm imm}(D)} Z_i \qquad\text{a.s.} \]
nodes.statement_short: Dominate N(D) by a compound sum of progenies

nodes.name: Mean bound
nodes.statement: Taking expectations gives \[ \mathbb{E} N(D)\ \le\ \mathbb{E} N^{\rm imm}(D)\,\mathbb{E} Z\ \le\ M_\Sigma^{\rm base}\,m_1\,|D|. \] Thus Assumption~\ref{ass:G0} holds with $C_{\rm act}:=M_\Sigma^{\rm base}m_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Expected activity is linear in |D|

nodes.name: Compound-Poisson mgf
nodes.statement: For the tail bound, use the compound-Poisson mgf: for any $\theta\in(0,\theta_0]$, \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\big[e^{\theta N(D)}\big] \ \le&\ \mathbb{E}\!\left[\exp\!\left(\theta\sum_{i=1}^{N^{\rm imm}(D)} Z_i\right)\right]\\ \ =&\ \exp\!\Big(\mathbb{E} N^{\rm imm}(D)\,( \mathbb{E}[e^{\theta Z}]-1)\Big)\\ \ \le&\ \exp\!\big(M_\Sigma^{\rm base}|D|\,(m_\theta-1)\big). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the mgf of N(D)

nodes.name: Chernoff bound
nodes.statement: A Chernoff bound yields, for any $x>0$, \[ \mathbb{P}\!\big(N(D)\ge x|D|\big) \ \le\ \exp\!\Big(-|D|\big(\theta x - M_\Sigma^{\rm base}(m_\theta-1)\big)\Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Chernoff tail bound

nodes.name: Exponential tail
nodes.statement: Since $x\mapsto \sup_{\theta\in(0,\theta_0]}(\theta x - M_\Sigma^{\rm base}(m_\theta-1))$ is strictly positive for all $x$ above the mean rate, there exist $\eta_{\rm act}\in(0,1)$ and $c>0$ such that taking $x=(1+\eta_{\rm act})C_{\rm act}$ gives the claimed $e^{-c|D|}$ bound for all large $|D|$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose x above the mean rate

nodes.name: Total counting measure
nodes.statement: Throughout the proof, constants may change from line to line but depend only on the Hawkes-process parameters, on $h,R$, and on the geometry of $\mathcal S$, not on $D$. Let $N_k$ be the marked counting measure for mark $k\in\{0,1\}$, and let \[ N := N_0 + N_1 \] be the total (unmarked) counting measure, so that for any Borel set $B\subset D$ we have $N(B)=N_0(B)+N_1(B)$.
nodes.statement_short: Conventions and the total counting measure
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Spatial aggregation
nodes.statement: For each $k\in\{0,1\}$, define the spatially aggregated (ground) process \[ \widetilde N_k(I) := N_k(I\times\mathcal{S}), \qquad I\subset\mathbb{R}\ \text{Borel}, \] and set \[ \widetilde N(I) := \widetilde N_0(I)+\widetilde N_1(I). \] Clearly, for any $(t,x)\in D$, \begin{equation} N\bigl([t-h,t]\times B_R(x)\bigr) \;\le\; \widetilde N\bigl([t-h,t]\bigr). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Aggregate in space; local counts are majorised (eq. 35)
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Aggregated intensity
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda_k(t,x)$ denote the intensity of $N_k$ at $(t,x)$, and let $\widetilde\lambda_k(t)$ be the intensity of $\widetilde N_k$: \[ \widetilde\lambda_k(t) = \int_{\mathcal{S}} \lambda_k(t,x)\,\mathrm{d}\mu(x). \] By the model definition and Fubini, \[ \widetilde\lambda_k(t) = \int_{\mathcal{S}} \mu_k(t,x)\,\mathrm{d}\mu(x) + \sum_{\ell=0}^1 \int_{(t-h,t)}\!\!\int_{\mathcal{S}}\!\int_{\mathcal{S}} g_{k\ell}(t-s,x-y)\,N_\ell(\mathrm{d} s,\mathrm{d} y)\,\mathrm{d}\mu(x). \]
nodes.statement_short: Compute the aggregated intensity by Fubini
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Envelope kernel bound
nodes.statement: For each pair $(k,\ell)$ and lag $u>0$, define the envelope kernel \[ \varphi^{\mathrm{env}}_{k\ell}(u) := \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} g_{k\ell}(u,z)\,\mathrm{d}\mu(z), \] and note that for any $y\in\mathcal{S}$, \[ \int_{\mathcal{S}} g_{k\ell}(u,x-y)\,\mathrm{d}\mu(x) \;\le\; \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} g_{k\ell}(u,z)\,\mathrm{d}\mu(z) \;=\; \varphi^{\mathrm{env}}_{k\ell}(u). \] Thus, using \(\mu(\mathcal{S})<\infty\), set \[ \overline\mu_k^{\rm agg} := \mu(\mathcal{S})\,\sup_{t\in[t^\ast,T],\,x\in\mathcal{S}} \mu_k(t,x) \ <\ \infty. \] Then \[ \widetilde\lambda_k(t) \;\le\; \overline\mu_k^{\rm agg} + \sum_{\ell=0}^1 \int_{(t-h,t)} \varphi^{\mathrm{env}}_{k\ell}(t-s)\, \widetilde N_\ell(\mathrm{d} s). \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound the aggregated intensity by an envelope kernel
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Temporal envelope Hawkes process
nodes.statement: Define the purely temporal \(2\)-dimensional linear Hawkes process \(\overline N=(\overline N_0,\overline N_1)\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) with baselines \(\overline\mu_k^{\rm agg}\) and interaction kernels \(\varphi^{\mathrm{env}}_{k\ell}\), i.e. \[ \overline\lambda_k(t) = \overline\mu_k^{\rm agg} + \sum_{\ell=0}^1 \int_{(t-h,t)} \varphi^{\mathrm{env}}_{k\ell}(t-s)\,\overline N_\ell(\mathrm{d} s). \] Its reproduction matrix is exactly $A=(A_{k\ell})$ as in Assumption~\ref{ass:H-stab}: \[ A_{k\ell} = \int_0^h \varphi^{\mathrm{env}}_{k\ell}(u)\,\mathrm{d} u = \int_0^h\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} g_{k\ell}(u,z)\,\mathrm{d}\mu(z)\,\mathrm{d} u. \]
nodes.statement_short: Define a temporal Hawkes envelope with the same reproduction matrix
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Poisson embedding
nodes.statement: Let $(\Pi_k)_{k\in\{0,1\}}$ be independent Poisson random measures on $[t^\ast,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}_+$ with intensity $dt\,dz$. We construct $\overline N$ by the standard Poisson embedding for (linear) Hawkes processes with nonnegative kernels; see, e.g., \cite[Proposition~14.7.I]{daley2007introduction}, \citet[Section~3]{bremaud1996stability}, and \citet{bremaud2002rate}: \[ \overline N_k(dt) :=\int_{\mathbb{R}_+}\mathbf 1_{\{z\le \overline\lambda_k(t-)\}}\, \Pi_k(dt,dz), \qquad \overline\lambda_k(t) =\overline\mu_k^{\rm agg}+\sum_\ell\int \varphi^{\rm env}_{k\ell}(t-s)\,\overline N_\ell(ds). \] On the same Poisson basis, define $\widetilde N$ analogously by \[ \widetilde N_k(dt) :=\int_{\mathbb{R}_+}\mathbf 1_{\{z\le \widetilde\lambda_k(t-)\}}\, \Pi_k(dt,dz), \] which is the coupled construction used in \cite[Lemma~3]{bremaud1996stability}.
nodes.statement_short: Couple both processes via a common Poisson embedding
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Monotone coupling
nodes.statement: Define the first-violation time \[ \tau:=\inf\Bigl\{t\ge t^\ast:\exists k \text{ with }\widetilde N_k([t^\ast,t])>\overline N_k([t^\ast,t])\Bigr\}. \] On $\{\tau>t\}$ we have $\widetilde N_\ell|_{[t^\ast,t)}\le \overline N_\ell|_{[t^\ast,t)}$ for all $\ell$, and hence, by the nonnegativity of $\varphi^{\rm env}$ (monotonicity of the linear Hawkes process map), \[ \widetilde\lambda_k(t-) \le \overline\mu_k^{\rm agg}+\sum_\ell \int \varphi^{\rm env}_{k\ell}(t-s)\,\widetilde N_\ell(ds) \le \overline\mu_k+\sum_\ell\int \varphi^{\rm env}_{k\ell}(t-s)\,\overline N_\ell(ds) =\overline\lambda_k(t-). \] Therefore the acceptance region for $\widetilde N_k$ is contained in that of $\overline N_k$ at time $t$ (cf.\ the monotone coupling argument in \citet{bremaud1996stability}), so $\tau=\infty$ almost surely and $\widetilde N\le \overline N$ pathwise. In particular, \begin{equation} \widetilde N_k(J)\le \overline N_k(J) \quad\text{for all Borel intervals }J\subset[t^\ast,\infty),\ \ k\in\{0,1\}. \end{equation} Intuitively, $\widetilde N$ is obtained by thinning the envelope $\overline N$ via the common Poisson embedding \cite[Proposition~14.7.I]{daley2007introduction}.
nodes.statement_short: First-violation argument gives pathwise domination (eq. 36)
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Stationary domination
nodes.statement: Because the kernels are nonnegative and $\xi(A)<1$, the process $\overline N$ admits a unique stationary version $\overline N^{\mathrm{stat}}$ on $\mathbb{R}$ \citep{bremaud1996stability}. Using the standard Poisson cluster representation, we may construct the empty-history envelope $\overline N$ on $[t^\ast,\infty)$ by removing all clusters whose ancestral point lies before $t^\ast$ from $\overline N^{\mathrm{stat}}$; hence, for any interval $J\subset[t^\ast,\infty)$, \begin{equation} \overline N_k(J) \;\le\; \overline N^{\mathrm{stat}}_k(J) \quad\text{a.s.} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Dominate by the stationary version (eq. 37)
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Window domination
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{eq:spatial-majorisation-app}, \eqref{eq:env-domination-app} and \eqref{eq:stationary-domination-app}, we obtain the pathwise bound \begin{equation} N\bigl([t-h,t]\times B_{R'}(x)\bigr) \;\le\; \overline N^{\mathrm{stat}}\bigl([t-h,t]\bigr) := \sum_{k=0}^1 \overline N^{\mathrm{stat}}_k\bigl([t-h,t]\bigr) \end{equation} for every $t\in[t^\ast,T]$, every $x\in\mathcal{S}$, and for every radius $R'\ge 0$ (since the right-hand side does not depend on $R'$).
nodes.statement_short: Combine into pathwise window domination (eq. 38)
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Single-window tail
nodes.statement: We next obtain an exponential tail bound for a single temporal window. The process $\overline N^{\mathrm{stat}}$ is a standard multivariate linear Hawkes process with nonnegative, compactly supported kernels and $\xi(A)<1$. Therefore, we can apply \cite[Proposition~2]{hansen2015lasso} to $\overline N^{\mathrm{stat}}$ on the interval $[-h,0)$: there exists $\theta>0$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}\bigl[\exp\bigl( \theta\,\overline N^{\mathrm{stat}}([-h,0))\bigr)\bigr] < \infty. \] By stationarity, for any interval $I$ of length $h$ we have \( \overline N^{\mathrm{stat}}(I) \stackrel{d}{=} \overline N^{\mathrm{stat}}([-h,0)). \) Fix such an interval $I$ and set \[ M := \mathbb{E}\bigl[\exp\bigl( \theta\,\overline N^{\mathrm{stat}}(I)\bigr)\bigr] < \infty. \] A Chernoff bound then gives \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}\bigl( \overline N^{\mathrm{stat}}(I) > n \bigr) \;\le\; M e^{-\theta n} \qquad\text{for all }n\ge 0. \end{equation} The constants $M$ and $\theta$ depend only on the Hawkes process parameters and on $h$, not on the particular choice of $I$.
nodes.statement_short: Exponential moment of the stationary Hawkes process gives a Chernoff tail (eq. 39)
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Time grid
nodes.statement: It remains to discretize $D$ and apply a union bound. Let $\Delta_t:=h/2$ and define \[ \mathsf{T} := \bigl\{t_i:=t^\ast+i\Delta_t:\ i=0,1,\dots,I_T\bigr\}, \quad I_T:=\Bigl\lceil\frac{T-t^\ast}{\Delta_t}\Bigr\rceil. \] Then \( |\mathsf{T}| \le 2\,(T-t^\ast)/h + 2 \le C_t (T-t^\ast)/h \) for some absolute constant $C_t$.
nodes.statement_short: Discretise time
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Spatial cover
nodes.statement: Because $\mathcal{S}\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is bounded, there exists a finite set $\mathcal X=\{x_1,\dots,x_J\}\subset\mathcal{S}$ such that \[ \mathcal{S} \subset \bigcup_{j=1}^J B_{R/2}(x_j). \] We keep $J$ implicit; it depends only on $\mathcal{S}$, $R$ and the dimension $d$, and in particular does not depend on the observation window $D$.
nodes.statement_short: Cover S by finitely many balls
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Space-time grid
nodes.statement: Set \[ \mathcal G := \mathsf{T}\times \mathcal X,\qquad |\mathcal G| = |\mathsf{T}|\,|\mathcal X| \;\le\; C_t J\,\frac{T-t^\ast}{h} \;=\; C_{\rm grid}\,|D| \] for some constant $C_{\rm grid}>0$ depending only on $h,R$ and the geometry of $\mathcal{S}$ (we used $|D|=(T-t^\ast)\,\mu(\mathcal{S})$ here).
nodes.statement_short: Grid of size O(|D|)
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Grid union bound
nodes.statement: For the covering/union-bound argument we work with enlarged spatial balls \(B_{2R}(y)\), so that any target ball \(B_R(x)\) is contained in some \(B_{2R}(y)\) from the spatial grid. For each $(s,y)\in\mathcal G$, consider the spacetime window \[ W_{s,y}:=[s-h,s]\times B_{2R}(y). \] By \eqref{eq:window-domination-app} (with radius $2R$) and \eqref{eq:single-window-tail-app}, we have \[ \mathbb{P}\bigl(N(W_{s,y})>n\bigr) \;\le\; \mathbb{P}\bigl(\overline N^{\mathrm{stat}}([s-h,s])>n\bigr) \;\le\; M e^{-\theta n} \] for every $(s,y)\in\mathcal G$ and all $n\ge 0$. A union bound over the finite grid $\mathcal G$ yields \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}\Bigl( \max_{(s,y)\in\mathcal G} N(W_{s,y})>n \Bigr) \;\le\; |\mathcal G|\,M e^{-\theta n} \;\le\; C_{\rm grid} M\,|D|\,e^{-\theta n}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Union bound over enlarged grid windows (eq. 40)
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Cover arbitrary windows
nodes.statement: For any $(t,x)\in D$, choose $s\in\mathsf{T}$ and $y\in\mathcal X$ such that \[ |t-s|\le \Delta_t = h/2,\qquad \|x-y\|\le R/2. \] Then $B_R(x)\subset B_{3R/2}(y)\subset B_{2R}(y)$ and \[ [t-h,t] \subset [s-2h,s+h]. \] The interval $[s-2h,s+h]$ is contained in the union of three intervals of length $h$, for example $[s-2h,s-h]$, $[s-h,s]$, and $[s,s+h]$. Hence \[ [t-h,t]\times B_R(x) \subset \bigcup_{\ell=1}^3 \bigl([s_\ell-h,s_\ell]\times B_{2R}(y)\bigr), \] for suitable $s_\ell\in\mathsf{T}'$ in a time grid $\mathsf{T}'$ obtained by shifting $\mathsf{T}$ by multiples of $h$. Enlarging $\mathcal G$ if necessary to \( \mathcal G':=\mathsf{T}'\times\mathcal X, \) we obtain \[ N\bigl([t-h,t]\times B_R(x)\bigr) \;\le\; 3\max_{(s,y)\in\mathcal G'} N\bigl([s-h,s]\times B_{2R}(y)\bigr). \] The cardinality of $\mathcal G'$ is still bounded by a constant multiple of $|D|$: $|\mathcal G'|\le C'_{\rm grid}|D|$ for some $C'_{\rm grid}>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Any window is covered by three grid windows
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Supremum bound
nodes.statement: Taking a supremum over $(t,x)\in D$ yields \[ \sup_{(t,x)\in D} N\bigl([t-h,t]\times B_R(x)\bigr) \;\le\; 3\max_{(s,y)\in\mathcal G'} N\bigl([s-h,s]\times B_{2R}(y)\bigr). \] Therefore, \[ \mathbb{P}\!\left( \sup_{(t,x)\in D} N\bigl([t-h,t]\times B_R(x)\bigr) > 3n \right) \;\le\; \mathbb{P}\!\left( \max_{(s,y)\in\mathcal G'} N\bigl([s-h,s]\times B_{2R}(y)\bigr) > n \right). \] Applying \eqref{eq:grid-union-app} (with $\mathcal G'$ and possibly a different grid constant) gives \[ \mathbb{P}\!\left( \sup_{(t,x)\in D} N\bigl([t-h,t]\times B_R(x)\bigr) > 3n \right) \;\le\; C''_{\rm grid} M\,|D|\,e^{-\theta n} \] for some $C''_{\rm grid}>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the supremum and apply the grid union bound
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Choose n_*
nodes.statement: Finally, let $\eta>0$ be arbitrary and choose \[ n = n_0(|D|) := \Bigl\lceil \frac{\eta+1}{\theta}\,\log|D| \Bigr\rceil. \] Then \[ C''_{\rm grid}M\,|D|\,e^{-\theta n} \;\le\; C''_{\rm grid}M\,|D|\,e^{-(\eta+1)\log|D|} \;=\; C''_{\rm grid}M\,|D|^{-\eta}. \] Absorbing the multiplicative constant $3$ in front of $n$ into the definition of $c_1(\eta)$ (i.e.\ replacing $n_0(|D|)$ by $3n_0(|D|)$) and renaming constants \[ c_1(\eta):=\frac{3(\eta+1)}{\theta}, \qquad c_2(\eta):=C''_{\rm grid}M, \] we obtain \[ n_*(|D|) := \bigl\lceil c_1(\eta)\,\log|D| \bigr\rceil \] Thus we have shown \(\mathbb{P}(\widetilde\Omega_{n_*}(h,R)^c)\le c_2(\eta)\,|D|^{-\eta}\). Since \(\Omega_{n_*}(h,R)^c\subseteq \widetilde\Omega_{n_*}(h,R)^c\), the same bound holds for \(\mathbb{P}(\Omega_{n_*}(h,R)^c)\).
nodes.statement_short: Choose n of order log|D| for a polynomial tail
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Fix objects
nodes.statement: Fix $\theta\in\Theta_\circ$ and a deterministic labelling $r$. Let $r^\star$ denote the true labelling on $D$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix theta, r and r*

nodes.name: Intensity formulas
nodes.statement: Under the Hawkes model specification, \begin{align*} \widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta) =& \mu_k(\tau;\theta)+\sum_{\ell=0}^1\int g_{k\ell}(\tau-\tau';\theta)\,d\widehat N_\ell^r(\tau'),\\ \lambda_k(\tau\mid\mathcal G_{t-};\theta) =& \mu_k(\tau;\theta)+\sum_{\ell=0}^1\int g_{k\ell}(\tau-\tau';\theta)\,d N_\ell(\tau'). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Write label-induced and oracle intensities

nodes.name: Oracle equals true-label intensity
nodes.statement: Under the stated conditioning (empty history or marked pre-$t^\ast$ history fixed), the marked past entering the Hawkes functional is the same in $\widehat\lambda^{r^\star}$ and in the oracle intensity, and moreover $\widehat N_\ell^{r^\star}=N_\ell$ on $D$. Therefore $\widehat\lambda_k^{r^\star}(\tau;\theta)=\lambda_k(\tau\mid\mathcal G_{t-};\theta)$ for a.e.\ $\tau\in D$, hence $\tilde s_\theta(\tau;r^\star)=s^{\rm or}_\theta(\tau)$.
nodes.statement_short: Under the conditioning, the r*-induced score is the oracle score

nodes.name: Local event count
